items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 20 at 12:57PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
We are monitoring the potential for a coastal storm around
Thursday of this week. There is high uncertainty with the track of
the storm as it could be anywhere from the Yukon Delta to Bering
Strait. Fortunately, it doesn't appear to be a storm that would
come with major impacts. However, there is a chance for minor
coastal impacts and high surf due to gusty southeast winds during
the first half of the storm, then west-northwest winds as the low
passes through. We will continue to update as neces
items.areas: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 20 at 12:12PM AKDT until July 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 80 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Central Arctic Plains and Western Arctic Plains.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
items.areas: Western Arctic Plains; Central Arctic Plains
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Young children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances as vehicle interiors can reach extreme
temperatures in as little as 10 minutes.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 20 at 11:55AM AKDT until July 21 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 35 to 45 mph with frequent gusts to around 55
mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Today, the area has received some appreciable
sunshine, & therefore, frequent wind gusts have, once again,
increased up to between 50 & 55 mph around the Texas Condo area
due to e
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 20 at 11:25AM AKDT until July 20 at 7:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to around 80 expected.

* WHERE...City of Hyder.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures have already increased into the
mid 70s this morning and will continue to increase into this
afternoon.
items.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear sunscreen and light loose
fitting clothing. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

Locations next to the ocean or glaciers will be cooler with a
stronger breeze in the afternoon.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 19 at 2:24PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Local reports and river gage data indicate a glacier dammed lake
release on the Kennicott River near McCarthy.  Water levels on the
Kennicott are currently rising and will continue to rise over the
next 24-48 hours, cresting at or prior to Monday evening.

At this time, the river is expected to crest below minor flood
stage.  Widespread flooding is not anticipated, although the
following hazards will be present:

-Significant water level rises (feet/day)
-Bank erosion: Fast moving water

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 19 at 11:43AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Yentna, Skwentna and Susitna River basins

* Tonight through Monday Night

the Susitna Valley through Monday Night.

expected to occur late Monday night into Tuesday for most streams
and rivers, including the Yentna at Lake Creek.
